system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-02-17, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bysbij4-fog-alert-uae-motorists-warned-low-visibility] ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): Both language versions exceed the UAE one-page limit. English is 174 GSM-7 characters, which makes 2 pages at 93 characters per page. Arabic is 192 UCS-2 characters, which makes 5 pages at 82 octets (about 41 characters) per page. Handsets may display only part of the alert, or display it fragmented. Fix: Shorten the English text to no more than 93 GSM-7 characters, avoiding extension-table characters. Shorten the Arabic text to no more than 41 UCS-2 characters (82 octets). Keep the hazard, area, end time and action, and drop the detailed start date and the source line if needed. If the Arabic cannot carry the hazard and action within one page, a person must decide whether a multi-page Arabic message is acceptable. [cites 3GPP TS 23.038 Alphabets and language-specific information, version 18.0.0 Release 18 (ETSI TS 123 038 V18.0.0), p.15] | Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): Neither language contains a protective action. The text describes only the hazard (fog, zero visibility), the area, the time and the source. So the first page, and the whole message, tells people what is happening but not what to do. Fix: In both languages, put a short action near the start, within the first (and only) page. For example, in English: 'Avoid driving; if you must, slow down and use low-beam lights.' Add an equivalent Arabic sentence. [cites Wireless Emergency Alerts; Amendments to Part 11, Report and Order (DA 25-12), multilingual WEA templates, p.21]

data.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in western UAE until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb
data.description: Drive with care, keep distance: fog, visibility may hit zero, west UAE until 10am Wed.
data.instruction: Drive with extreme caution, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and follow modified speed limits in thick fog. Follow all traffic safety guidelines.
left_out: Reviewer's example action 'avoid driving; use low-beam lights': not in the verified NCM statement, so I used NCM's own advice instead.

Start time (21:30 Tue 17 Feb), full date and source line: dropped from the phone text to fit one 93-character GSM-7 page, as the reviewer allowed. The start time appears only in the headline area context, not in the description.
Issuer site https://alerts.example.ae: left out of the phone text for length.

Arabic version: not drafted here because this task asks for one English alert. The 41-character one-page Arabic text still needs a translator and a human decision on whether a multi-page Arabic message is acceptable.
data.note_for_reviewer: The phone text is 86 GSM-7 characters with no extension-table characters, and the action comes first. Please confirm that 'west UAE' fits the operator's Western region zone, and that 'until 10am Wed' is clear enough without the 18 Feb date.
